attribution.note: Zitron wrote this in his own first-person voice on his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'I think' comes with firm 'will never' language and no probability hedge, so this is a forecast. Rendering 'a lot of' as 'many' is fair. The 'trash' opinion is rightly left out.

contract.note: The contract fairly separates delay, loss of a tenant and permanent abandonment, and it invents no numeric threshold. The cohort and the meaning of 'paid' are evaluator readings, as the contract itself flags.

evidence.note: Dated before the evaluation date. Microsoft pulled out of Nscale's Loughton site, but Nscale says it remains committed. One withdrawal does not show permanent abandonment or nonpayment across a substantial set of deals.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The early-resolution rule needs permanent termination or nonpayment records across a clearly substantial, identifiable set of deals. The packet has one customer withdrawal from a project that is still being pursued, so the forecast is not yet settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'all', 'remarkably' and the 'appears to be' hedge on deceleration. The compound causal claims are stated faithfully, although the source's grammar on the 'glacial pace' clause is garbled.

contract.note: The plain reading (profit after financing costs, with 2025 as the latest full year) is ordinary and fair. The contract correctly requires evidence for the causal link, not just NVIDIA's market-cap rank.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's 10-K shows a large, rising interest burden at one operator. It does not show that debt makes all AI data centers remarkably unprofitable.

A company disclosure showing Microsoft and Meta among major customers. This weakens the 'customers are AI startups' characterization for one operator, but it is not a representative dataset of customers.
Capacity under construction in North America fell, while total capacity and absorption grew strongly. The release neither confirms nor rebuts deceleration as against NVIDIA's sales.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no project-level profit accounts across the sector, no representative data on customer losses, no dated market-cap record and no analysis linking construction to NVIDIA's valuation. Single-operator and pipeline data cannot settle the bundled causal claims.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Broad present-tense negative causal claim. 'Poisonous to the future' is evaluative. The testable parts are productivity, learning and effectiveness. The drafter's version drops 'all they do is prompt', but that is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading this as a broad negative causal assessment is ordinary and fair. The contract rightly separates learning, skill loss and output, and treats the language about the industry's future as unmeasurable.

evidence.note: An RCT found a slowdown with early-2025 tools in one setting. METR itself now says these results are out of date, so they do not describe AI as of March 2026. Learning is not measured.
An RCT found speed gains with Google's internal tools in summer 2024. That is an earlier period and a narrow task, so it cannot settle the 2026 characterization.
The closest data in time shows weak raw signs of a speedup with late-2025 tools, but the authors say selection effects make it unreliable.

reviews.rationale: The claim describes AI as of March 2026. Both controlled studies measure earlier tools in narrow coding settings, pointing in opposite directions, and the current-period data is unreliable. Nothing measures learning or unaided effectiveness, or costs against benefits. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully keeps 'I cannot find' and the age clause. It bundles three separate assertions (the 100 MW concept's age, the search for a gigawatt site, OpenAI's bills), and each needs different evidence.

contract.note: The contract treats the search as weaker than a claim of absence and reads 'pay its bills' as ability to meet obligations when due. Both are ordinary, fair readings.

evidence.note: A 2011 trade report describes a 100 MW data center design about fifteen years before the post. That meets the contract's test for contradicting the 'barely a few years old' component.
Epoch's November 2025 piece is a forecast of gigawatt sites coming online, not a commissioning record, so it does not settle operating status on March 24.
OpenAI's own announcement of $110B in new investment. It speaks to access to capital, but it does not show cash available against bills due.
A secondary report of about $40B in cash at the end of 2025. With no matched schedule of obligations, it does not settle whether OpenAI could pay in March.

reviews.rationale: The age component is contradicted: a 100 MW data center design was documented in 2011, well before 'a few years' ago. The gigawatt-search and OpenAI-bills components remain unresolved because no commissioning or matched liquidity records are in the packet. No component is supported, so the bundled claim fails on its age assertion.
